findings.title: busy() inferred from ticket error is fragile
findings.message: The goroutine reads s.closed and s.ticket and writes other Session state only inside the Publish callback, which is fine. But busy() relies on ticket.Err()==nil to mean in-flight; after the ticket completes or aborts without Publish running, behavior depends on Err semantics. A published-but-undrained ticket also reports busy only if Err is nil, so an overlapping request could pass in the gap, which risks double reservation.
findings.suggestion: Track in-flight state explicitly on the owner: set a boolean when reserving and clear it in the Publish callback and in Close, rather than inferring it from ticket.Err().

findings.title: Chooser closes channel on every call
findings.message: Tests read s.ticket and s.Field.Path from the test goroutine while the worker goroutine is running; the worker only touches captured locals, so this is OK, but the test closes `c.finished` via defer in ChoosePath, which panics on a second call (for example the drop test with a swapped chooser, or a repeat call). Fragile under -race and reuse.
findings.suggestion: Use sync.Once for closing finished, or create a fresh channel per call.
